newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI sale a giant leap for black business.
newsitem.headline: JCI sale a giant leap for black business.

text.p: Black South African business took a giant leap forward on Tuesday with the purchase of a controlling 34.9 percent stake JCI Ltd for 2.88 billion rand.
The deal is the second major disposal by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, South Africa's biggest company, to black interests.
"The main thrust in these cases is to make our contribution to black empowerment," Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said on Tuesday, announcing the JCI deal.
Anglo recently disposed of its 35 percent stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) -- an industrial holding concern -- to the National Empowerment Consortium, a black business grouping.
That deal gave blacks control or influence over companies representing nearly a tenth of the capitalisation of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
A new consortium, African Mining Group, led by Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd, is acquiring a 34.9 percent stake in JCI in a deal which mirrors many aspects of the Johnnic sale.
As in the Johnnic deal, Anglo will retain an interest, holding some 12 percent of JCI.
The consortium is paying 54.50 rand a share for the JCI stake, with payment due at the end of February, a 5.50 rand premium to JCI closing price on the stock exchange on Tuesday.
The JCI deal will see one of the gems of South africa's pivotal mining industry pass into black hands -- in a major symbol of change in post-apartheid South Africa.

The deal is also a major coup for Capital Alliance, a relative newcomer to the financial scene, which last month signed up Mark Barnes, formerly deputy managing director and head of treasury at Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank, as its chief executive.
